Summary
Jack, stationed in the Western Pacific, writes to his family in Brisbane, expressing his enjoyment of receiving their letters and his intention to print future letters for easier readability. He mentions visiting ruins and attending Army shows or movies, and expresses hope for the return of many soldiers. He asks the recipients to pass on his greetings and to keep in touch.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_35a) --- Dear Folks: Just received Ruth's last letter of 23 June. I enjoyed it very much. Getting mail here is a little more important than it was in Brisbane. I am trying to write a little plainer than I usually do so that you will be able to read this letter without any outside help. In fact, I think I will start printing my letters beginning next time so they will be easier to read. The letters AFWESPAC stand for Army Forces in Western Pacific. One of these days it will read AFJAP or army forces in Japan. How long have you been here? We have been here for a very long time. I have been around the ruins for about an hour and talk—and then [illegible] --- Page 2 (Beckerman_35b) --- We go to some Army show or movie. I get a big kick out of going around with him and listening to him talk. It was wonderful to hear about so many of our boys coming home. Please say hello to every- body for me and ask them to drop me a line. Good night Love Jack
